text:
sylvia: heads up, we started seeing a p99 spike out of ARN (~Stockholm) POP at 03:10 UTC, p99 ~420-480ms, throughput dropped ~18%. alerting spike from latency-monitor. anyone oncall?

infra-bot: [ALERT] arn-pop latency p99 > 400ms for 12m. graph: https://internal/graphs/arn/p99?range=30m incident_id=I-9321

josh: on it. pulling traces now, looks like a bunch of requests hit long queue_delay before kernel selection. grabbing profiler.

josh: top of pprof (cpu) shows heavy time in slow_path_dispatch and memcpy fallback in our custom kernel selector. snippet: `cpu_seconds: slow_path_dispatch 62%`, `kernel_choice: fallback=soft`

maria: tcpdump from a noisy host in arn shows repeated retransmits to 10.4.2.1 (provider NAT). sample: `08:12:33.123456 IP 10.4.2.45 > 10.4.2.1: Flags [P.], seq 1:1025, ack 1, win 64240, length 1024` then `08:12:33.223789 IP 10.4.2.1 > 10.4.2.45: RST` and retransmit counters jump.

ben: could be SNAT queueing / rate limit on provider side. saw something similar in SFO with aggregated NAT sessions starving tcp windows. can you check `conntrack -S` and `ss -s` on one of the affected hosts?

josh: ran conntrack, delta: `entries=124567 used=0.89 peak=124990`, but `nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established` looks fine. however provider counters show `nat_reasm_failed` + high `tx_queue_len` on eth0.

maria: kv-cache miss-rate spiked at same time: `kv_cache_miss_rate` from 2% -> 19% at 03:11. That lines up w/ requests taking longer, so batching waits longer and then falls back to small kernels.

josh: batching heuristic logged `batch_wait_ms` rising from 6 -> 50ms for many routes, and kernel-selector log shows `chosen_kernel: vectorized_fast` then `fallback: scalar_copy` for same request ids. fallback correlation with retransmits is high.

sylvia: suspect provider NAT/egress queueing is causing delayed ACKs/packet loss which inflates request RTT, hurting batching windows -> smaller batches -> more per-token CPU and kernel fallback.

ben: agreed. quick mitigation: route around provider NAT via alternate egress LB. Can we divert a small % to eu2-arn-eu-west2-egress? Dan, can you open a canary route?

dan: doing canary now. `infractl route set --pop arn --egress eu2-arn-egress --percent 5` -> executing.

infra-bot: Rollout started: 5% traffic to eu2-arn-egress. monitor: https://internal/rollouts/arn-canary/2234567890

josh: after 5m of canary: p99 on canary hosts ~95ms, core arn hosts still ~430ms. conntrack counters on canary show no nat_reasm failures. kv_cache_miss_rate on canary stayed ~3%.

maria: canary traces show kernel-selector stayed on vectorized_fast with stable batch_wait_ms ~7ms.

sylvia: that nails it -> egress NAT queueing at provider. plan: escalate to provider with tcpdump and conntrack samples, ramp canary to 30% and then shift traffic. Also add temporary kernel-selector override to prefer vectorized kernels under elevated rpc latency to reduce CPU cost while we shift.

ben: agreed. provider ticket inbound with packet captures and timestamps. I'm going to open T-4598 and ping account team.

josh: short-term patch: `KERNEL_SELECTOR_FORCE=vectorized_fast` toggle applied to arn hot pool (staged). command: `kubectl set env deploy/ri-runtime -n arn KERNEL_SELECTOR_FORCE=vectorized_fast --record`

eve: applied on 20% of hot pool nodes, monitoring CPU and p99. initial look: p99 dropped from 430 -> 210ms on patched nodes, but CPU token utilization up ~12%. acceptable until we fully shift egress.

sylvia: timeline: 03:10 detect, 03:18 canary route, 03:25 provider contacted, 03:30 kernel override staged, 03:40 ramping traffic to alt-egress -> target full traffic shift by 04:10 UTC, then revert override after provider fix.

maria: leaving some artifacts: tcpdump, conntrack outputs, kernel logs, kvcache histograms uploaded to incident bucket s3://redwood-incidents/arn/2234567890/

josh: followup actions: (1) detect egress queueing earlier via nat_reasm metric alert, (2) add automated canary egress path when nat_reasm > X, (3) make kernel-selector fallback less aggressive when kv_cache_miss_rate spikes, (4) postmortem once provider confirms root cause.

sylvia: thanks team. I'll own postmortem and customer impact notes. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Incident I-9321 updated: status=mitigated, note="traffic shifted to alternate egress and kernel override applied, provider engaged"
